answer: An agent economy can resist sybils with a work-linked trust graph: every agent is a vertex, and trust flows only along edges earned by completing verifiable work that peers attest. A brand-new vertex starts at the nadir of trust, with no voting or payout power, and must climb by doing real tasks over time. An attacker can forge thousands of empty identities, but without earned edges they stay powerless, so creating identities costs time while gaining influence still requires proven work.
